messages:
maya: quick heads-up — I opened a tiny PR to clarify how we treat 429 vs 503 in the error-ref. It also adds an SDK snippet for parsing Retry-After and a short note about fallback model selection. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412

sam: nice. can you add an explicit example for clients that get a numeric Retry-After vs HTTP-date? we keep getting questions about that in onboarding.

maya: yep, added both JS + Python examples in the snippet section. the JS one shows parseInt and Date fallback, python shows email-like parsing using email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime.

kevin: can you paste the JS snippet here? i want to sanity-check the behavior for sub-second backoff before i review the PR.

maya: sure —

maya: ```js
// parse Retry-After header (simple)
const ra = res.headers['retry-after'];
let delaySec = 1;
if (ra) {
  const n = parseInt(ra, 10);
  if (!Number.isNaN(n)) { delaySec = Math.max(1, n); } else {
    const t = Date.parse(ra);
    if (!Number.isNaN(t)) { delaySec = Math.max(1, Math.ceil((t - Date.now()) / 1000)); }
  }
}
setTimeout(() => retry(), delaySec * 1000);
```

lina: looks fine. maybe add a short note: treat anything < 1s as 1s to avoid tight-spin. you already did that but call it out explicitly in the prose.

olivia: also suggest adding a sample mapping table: when to retry vs when to fallback. e.g., 429 -> retry with backoff, 503 -> consider fallback to cheaper model/region or degraded features.

maya: added table in the PR description and a small flowchart image (inline). flowchart files are in the PR branch.

sam: is there any risk of calling fallback automatically for all 503s? some infra transient 503s are self-healing and we prefer quick retry. we should recommend a policy: try N retries over exponential backoff, then fallback.

kevin: +1. propose: for 503/504, do up to 3 retries with exponential backoff (base 0.5s, cap 8s), then fallback. for 429, honor Retry-After if present, otherwise exponential up to 60s cap. put concretes in the runbook.

maya: updated wording and added an example config block for SDKs under "fallback policies":

maya: ```yaml
fallback_policy:
  max_retries: 3
  base_backoff_ms: 500
  max_backoff_ms: 8000
  retry_on: [503,504,429]
  fallback_to: [gpt-small-quant, gpt-tiny]
  trim_context_before_fallback: true
```

lina: tiny nit — use snake_case or kebab consistently across docs. our SDK config samples are mostly snake_case.

maya: good catch. switched to snake_case in PR.

docs-bot: PR 412 updated — reviewers requested: @kevin, @lina, @sam. CI: docs-lint passed, images uploaded. :rocket:

sam: i'll do a quick pass tonight. kevin — if you can confirm the JS snippet doesn't encourage tight loops, then we can merge tomorrow morning.

kevin: skimmed — add one small defensive check: if Retry-After is a very large date in the future (like >7d), treat as 1h and surface to the team instead of sleeping forever. i'll comment inline.

maya: added that clamp and a short troubleshooting note: "If clients observe unusually long Retry-After values, raise with infra team — might indicate clock skew or misconfigured ratelimiter."

olivia: can we also add an internal cross-link to the runtime fallback feature doc (eng-runtime)? new customers keep asking how model variants are chosen.

maya: linked to eng-runtime/fallbacks.md and added a short excerpt explaining model variant compatibility rules.

lina: thanks — last thing: update the examples index so search picks up the new snippets under "429/retry-patterns". otherwise people miss it.

maya: done. i also added a short changelog entry for the docs release note.

sam: perfect. once kevin's inline done, merge. i'll add a small blurb to the weekly release notes. :+1:

kevin: left 2 inline comments. nothing blocking.

maya: merging after CI finishes. thanks all!
